title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
abstract: arXiv:2611.33943v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent skills are directories of instructions, reference materials, and scripts loaded on demand by coding agents. According to SkillsBench, although human-curated skills can raise the passing rate by about 16.6 percentage points (pp) on average, they have actually reduced the results for some tasks. Later research has started to gate or eliminate skills according to the above per-task gains. We have audited the above benchmark at the source-code level and analysed 7,554 public trials to form 1,421 paired "(configuration, task) cells". Source-code audit identified two controlled-verified cases of grader dependence and one operational definition gap; the average lift on these three tasks was 74.6 pp, and the overall average lift for the full set was 18.7 pp. The audit also found that four tasks contained placeholder skill directories, and a certain execution harness additionally added 48 built-in skills in most runs. translated_title: Skill Lift 到底衡量的是什么？对 SkillsBench 的源代码级审计与噪声感知重分析
translated_abstract: 智能体技能是编程智能体按需加载的指令、参考资料和脚本所组成的目录。根据 SkillsBench 的报告，尽管人工策划的技能平均可将通过率提高约 16.6 个百分点（pp），但它们实际上在某些任务上反而降低了成绩。后续研究已开始依据上述每任务收益来门控或剔除技能。我们在源代码层面对该基准进行了审计，并分析了 7,554 次公开试验，形成 1,421 个配对的“（配置，任务）”单元格。源代码审计发现了两例经对照验证的评分器依赖问题和一个操作性定义缺口；这三个任务上的平均提升为 74.6 pp，而完整任务集的总体平均提升为 18.7 pp。审计还发现四个任务包含占位符技能目录，且某个执行框架在大多数运行中额外注入了 48 个内置技能。没有任务层面的降低……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文对 SkillsBench 进行源代码级审计并对 7,554 次公开试验做噪声感知重分析，发现部分“技能提升”分数实际上源于评分器依赖和操作性定义缺口等测量缺陷，并将总体平均提升修正为 18.7 pp。
en_tdlr: This paper conducts a source-code-level audit of SkillsBench and a noise-aware reanalysis of 7,554 public trials, revealing that some reported "skill lift" scores stem from grader dependence and operational definition gaps rather than genuine skill benefits, revising the overall average lift to 18.7 pp.
